members.tone: Maximally blunt - leaves no room for hope or softening.

members.gloss: no longer having or seeming to have or expecting to have life
members.tone: The plain word. Direct and unsoftened; every other word in this family exists to avoid it.

members.gloss: deprived of life; no longer living
members.tone: Clinical and detached: it names the absence of life rather than mourning it.
The neutral official term - legal forms and medical records, no feeling either way.
Respectful and gentle - names the death while keeping the person in view.
A euphemism for dead. It softens the statement rather than praising the person.
Soft and everyday - what people say when 'dead' is too hard to say.
The most consoling form - reframes death as rest and the end of suffering.
Gravestone language - comfort offered to the living.
The gentlest euphemism - death softened into rest.

members.gloss: not having enough money to pay for necessities
members.tone: Temporary and undramatic - short of money this month, not poor in life.
Casual - out of money right now, a state rather than a condition.
British slang, cheerfully blunt.

members.gloss: having little money or few possessions
members.tone: The plain word for a lasting condition - factual, and heavy for being so plain.

members.gloss: not having enough money to pay for necessities
members.tone: Genteel and bookish - poverty at a polite distance.

members.gloss: not having enough money to pay for necessities
members.tone: Absolute and vivid - not a coin left.

members.gloss: poor enough to need help from others
members.tone: Frames poverty as requiring help; of a person's temperament it means something else entirely.

members.gloss: poor enough to need help from others
members.tone: Made poor - the word implies something was taken away.

members.gloss: poor enough to need help from others
members.tone: The legal and administrative term for qualifying poverty.

members.gloss: poor enough to need help from others
members.tone: Total and grave - without even the means to live.

members.gloss: poor enough to need help from others
members.tone: Poverty as an affliction that has struck, not a state chosen.
Willing to try - courage as good sportsmanship rather than heroism.
Courage as endurance - staying in when it hurts.
Affectionate praise for spirit - the courage is admired rather than feared.

members.gloss: possessing or displaying courage; able to face and deal with danger or fear without flinching
members.tone: The plain, universal praise - facing what frightens you.

members.gloss: possessing or displaying courage; able to face and deal with danger or fear without flinching
members.tone: Weightier than 'brave' - implies moral choice, not just nerve.
Chivalrous courage - noble and old-fashioned.
Heroic register, at home in battle and legend.
Courage defined by what failed to stop it.
The superlative - courage as legend.

members.gloss: showing extreme courage; especially of actions courageously undertaken in desperation as a last resort
members.tone: Courage beyond what could be asked of anyone.

members.gloss: lacking conviction or boldness or courage
members.tone: Soft censure - the courage is missing, but the word pities more than it blames.

members.gloss: lacking conviction or boldness or courage
members.tone: Lacking boldness - the mildest word in the family, closer to pity than contempt.

members.gloss: lacking courage; ignobly timid and faint-hearted
members.tone: Cowardice named as a fault of character, not a passing fear.

members.gloss: lacking courage; ignobly timid and faint-hearted
members.tone: The plain accusation - fear that led to failing others.
Playground taunt - mocking rather than grave.
Dated, theatrical scorn - the pale liver standing in for a missing spine.
Blunt slang accusation of cowardice.

members.gloss: lacking even the rudiments of courage; abjectly fearful
members.tone: Abject cowardice - formal and thoroughly contemptuous.
Cowardice joined to malice - the blow struck from safety.

members.gloss: lacking in courage and manly strength and resolution; contemptibly fearful
members.tone: Bookish contempt - small-spirited in the face of difficulty.

members.gloss: lacking even the rudiments of courage; abjectly fearful
members.tone: Abject cowardice - formal and thoroughly contemptuous.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: Crude and flippant - it reduces a death to a joke.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: British slang, jokey and dismissive.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: A comic idiom - keeps death at arm's length by making light of it.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: Abrupt and unsentimental - emphasises the suddenness.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: Casual to the point of dismissive.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: Military slang - gallows humour rather than disrespect.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: The plain, honest verb - direct without being cruel.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: Grave and literary - deaths in numbers, or deaths that should not have happened.
Death framed as losing a long fight - respectful of the struggle.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: Clinical and detached - the word on a chart, not at a graveside.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: Legal register: the death is an event on a form.

members.gloss: die, as in battle or in a hunt
members.tone: A soft, dignifying word for a death in the field - soldier or quarry, the fall sounds fated rather than inflicted.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: The standard gentle phrase - what you say to someone who has just lost a person.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: Even shorter and softer than 'pass away' - the gentlest form of the euphemism.

members.gloss: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
members.tone: Grand phrasing for an ordinary end, which is why it turns comic.

members.gloss: characteristic of or befitting a friend
members.tone: The unarguable positive: it describes behaviour nobody objects to and implies nothing further.
Easy, unforced warmth of manner - friendliness that costs its owner nothing.
Mild, slightly old-fashioned praise; pleasantness rather than depth.
Warmth actively given off - genial, easy friendliness that puts people at ease.
Warmth that puts a room at ease.

members.gloss: (used colloquially) having the relationship of friends or pals
members.tone: Faintly disapproving of other people's friendships - it hints the closeness came too fast or too conveniently.

members.gloss: (used colloquially) having the relationship of friends or pals
members.tone: British and blokeish: friendly in a way that insists on being equals.

members.gloss: (used colloquially) having the relationship of friends or pals
members.tone: It raises an eyebrow at a friendship that looks more like an arrangement.

members.gloss: (used colloquially) having the relationship of friends or pals
members.tone: Openly mocking - the reduplication does the sneering for you.
Technical and cool - it describes the fit, not the affection.
Hearty warmth between equals - friendliness declared out loud rather than implied.
Heartiness offered to everyone alike - friendliness worn as a manner.
Backhanded: friendly to everyone, and so to no one in particular.
Scots for a cosy, unforced warmth; affectionate and close to untranslatable.
A spelling of 'couthie', with the same Scots warmth.

members.gloss: having or fostering a warm or friendly and informal atmosphere
members.tone: Of an atmosphere rather than a person - warmth kept at a small and informal scale.

members.gloss: (used of persons and their behavior) cultivated and genteel
members.tone: Praises taste without naming what it consists of - which is how it also flatters the speaker's own.

members.gloss: marked by refinement in taste and manners

members.gloss: marked by refinement in taste and manners

members.gloss: marked by refinement in taste and manners
members.tone: Praises the work, not the birth - it says the taste was acquired on purpose.

members.gloss: marked by refinement in taste and manners
members.tone: Warmer and less effortful than cultivated; it suggests taste that was absorbed rather than studied.

members.gloss: marked by refinement in taste and manners
members.tone: Refinement praised, but primly - the word can carry a faintly pitying edge, as in 'shabby-genteel'.

members.gloss: marked by refinement in taste and manners
members.tone: Not courtesy but cultivation - the refinement a whole circle credits itself with.
The joke is in the word itself - refinement praised with one eyebrow raised.
Mocks refinement as performance - the daintiness is put on.
Pure contempt - the invented, mincing sound does the sneering.
Disapproves gently: correct manners held so tightly they have become a fault.
British and withering - sweetness pushed past charm into embarrassment.

members.gloss: willing to give and share unstintingly
members.tone: The plain, unqualified praise - it credits both the giving and the spirit behind it.

members.gloss: generous in providing aid to others
members.tone: Praises the disposition rather than any particular gift.

members.gloss: generous in providing aid to others
members.tone: Warm - the giving is presented as coming from feeling, not duty.
Praise with a shrug - 'big of you' can be sincere or sarcastic.
Entirely sincere - it praises the person, not the sum.
Biblical in flavour - generosity on a grand scale.
Abundance more than kindness - the giving is a matter of plenty.
Describes the habit of giving easily, with no comment on why.
Praises the scale of the giving, and implies it exceeded what was owed.
Slightly therapeutic in register; it names a personality type rather than an act.
Abundance framed as generosity - the giving is ample rather than measured.
A vivid old word: the hand is not closed, and neither is the person.

members.gloss: tenaciously unwilling or marked by tenacious unwillingness to yield
members.tone: Refusal held past the point of reason - the word faults the persistence.

members.gloss: tenaciously unwilling or marked by tenacious unwillingness to yield
members.tone: Colder and more formal than stubborn; it withholds the affection stubborn allows.

members.gloss: tenaciously unwilling or marked by tenacious unwillingness to yield
members.tone: The refusal is a refusal to be reformed, and the speaker has given up on it.

members.gloss: stubbornly obstructive and unwilling to cooperate
members.tone: British and furious - it says the obstruction is the whole point.

members.gloss: stubbornly obstructive and unwilling to cooperate
members.tone: Almost fond, in the way one is fond of a difficult relative; the word is too comic to wound.
Frames the refusal as insubordination rather than character - mutinous, not merely difficult.
British; it makes the defiance sound adolescent, which is the insult.
Adds stupidity to the charge - not just unmoving but unable to see why it should move.
The same accusation with a harder image, and unkind about the head as well.
The most contemptuous of the stubborn words: obstinacy treated as stupidity.
The same refusal to yield, entirely admired - dogged is what stubborn is called when it wins.
Unyielding and unsmiling; it judges the manner as much as the will.

members.gloss: not in action or at work
members.tone: Describes the state, not the person - machinery and money are idle too.
British and total: the laziness is presented as going all the way through.
The same accusation in the plainer word; no part of the person is exempted.
A do-nothing word for a do-nothing; it condemns from a distance.
The softest of the real accusations - it sounds almost like a temperament.
The everyday charge, and a moral one: the work was there and was not done.
Idleness stated with Latinate coolness - disinclination to effort, judged from a height.
Names one of the seven deadly sins; the laziness is a fault of the soul.
Accusing - unwillingness to work treated as a character fault, not a circumstance.

members.gloss: idle or indolent especially in a dreamy way
members.tone: Comic rather than damning; the failing is a lack of spirit, not of will.
Idleness admired - because it is assumed to have been paid for.
Purely factual: not currently occupied, with no view taken on why.
The plain word, and the honest one: approval expressed and meant.
Archaic and hearty - praise sung out in a full round voice.
Borrows the gesture from the military; it praises formally and briefly, as an act of respect.

members.gloss: express that something is worthy of praise
members.tone: Public by nature - the praise is performed so that others see it given.
Ceremonial - it lifts the praise onto a formal, liturgical register.
Praise at length and without reservation - the enthusiasm is part of the meaning.
Raises the subject rather than merely approving of them; close to worship.
Praise raised toward worship - and it turns accusatory the moment the object does not deserve it.
About the volume, not the sincerity: praise announced rather than felt.
Praise with a purpose: the compliment is a means to something.
Flattery with coaxing added - the praise is a lever being worked.
Ceremonial praise, expected by the occasion, which discounts it slightly.
The British spelling of the same funeral-shaped praise.

members.gloss: say something to someone that expresses praise
members.tone: Small, direct and social - one remark, given to a person's face.
